summary: The hook sends a reply back when a generator ran after the user named existing inputs and the reply does not say whether the generator used them.
doc: This Stop hook blocks only when three conditions occur in the same turn: the prompt names something that already exists, a generator command runs, and the reply contains no sentence stating whether the generator used the named input. A generator is a script or API that makes new output from a prompt. Words such as regenerated, re-rendered or at native size describe a process, so they do not state whether the named input was used. A sentence such as "I did not use the two images you looked at; these are new ones" clears the hook. When the generator made unrelated output, npx guardhooks declare substitution-disclosure-stop "<what it made and why it replaced nothing>" records a two-hour exception. Your generator entry points can go in <config>/guardhooks/generator-commands.txt. The hook blocks at most once per turn and three times per session.
